findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I found no blocking errors in the four test improvements, and each one tests what it claims. (1) Mixed cleanup now adds an unrelated project's marker to the fixture. It takes the before and after snapshots of the Claude config with the same single-path exclusion (`snapshotClaudeConfig` with the current project). It also checks the fake-claude state file, a clean current marker, and that no pending transaction file remains. A cleanup that touches any other profile file would therefore fail. (2) Declined cleanup reuses `assertNoClaudeMutationCalls`. The fake `claude` appends every argv to its log before any simulated failure, so attempts that fail are still caught. Profile and project snapshots are also compared in full, with no exclusion. (3) The catalogue test now loops over every generated `skills/*/SKILL.md`. For each one it requires exactly one inventory entry, a 64-hex `skill_sha256`, and equality with `claudeSkillSha256` computed on the generated (adapted) bytes. It would catch a missing field, a hash taken over pre-adaptation content, or a duplicate entry. (4) The desktop-normalization dispatcher test first confirms the YAML rewrite actually changed the skill. It then compares the proof file, keyed by the canonical project root, against the exact expected record (version, manifest digest, canonical plugin root, event, session) and checks that the timestamp is in ISO form. The context notes that production code was not changed. The remaining findings are non-blocking warnings about blind spots and how strong the proof is.

`snapshotDirectory` and `snapshotDirectoryExcept` only record regular files (`filesBeneath` skips symlinks and empty directories). So a cleanup that creates an empty directory or a symlink under the Claude config or the project would still pass the 'byte-identical' checks. That is narrower than the scenario wording ('the Claude profile outside the current project's plugin-mode marker is byte-identical').

The skill-digest catalogue test calls the same `claudeSkillSha256` function the generator uses. It proves the generated inventory uses that function on the final adapted bytes, but it cannot catch a semantic bug inside `claudeSkillSha256` itself. That relies on the dispatcher tests: the normalized header is accepted, and changed metadata or body is rejected. Those tests currently cover only `skills/audit/SKILL.md`.

'Declines cleanup confirmation' is simulated by running `claude cleanup --json --no-input` without `--yes`. No interactive prompt is driven or answered 'no'. That is reasonable for the deterministic lane, but it is a preview path, not an actual decline. If an interactive confirmation prompt is ever added, this test would not cover it.

In the mixed-cleanup scenario, `'user-authored, third-party, Cursor-shared, and project-owned assets are byte-identical'` checks only specific known files plus a regex match on the settings theme. The full project tree is not re-snapshotted after cleanup. This is acceptable because the scenario expects cleanup to change project files. The new profile-side exclusion snapshot is the stronger of the two checks.

The verification note says that more integrity fault probes and independent review are still pending, and it limits its claims to simulated process-boundary proof. No authenticated desktop host coverage is claimed, so the claims do not exceed the proof.
